name: allocate_icon_record
description: Allocates a 96-byte memory block through a library call and, if that succeeds, stores the value 10 in the block and in the caller's buffer before passing both to a second library routine. Returns whether the allocation succeeded.

name: return_constant_zero
description: Returns zero with no other work, so the caller receives a false or failure status.

name: check_result_matches_fourth_argument
description: Passes three of its arguments to a second library routine and returns that routine's result if it equals the last argument, otherwise returns zero.

name: return_without_action
description: Returns immediately without any work, so calling it has no effect.

name: check_result_matches_fourth_argument
description: Passes three of its arguments to a second library routine and returns that routine's result if it equals the last argument, otherwise returns zero.

name: return_without_action
description: Returns immediately without any work, so calling it has no effect.

name: divide_32_bit_values
description: Divides a 32-bit unsigned value by a divisor: when the divisor is larger than 16 bits it uses sixteen shift-and-subtract steps, otherwise it uses two 16-bit divisions. The quotient and remainder are returned together in a 64-bit result.

name: divide_by_shift_subtract
description: Runs sixteen shift-and-subtract steps that move the dividend bits through a running remainder, subtracting the divisor and setting a quotient bit whenever the remainder reaches it. The quotient and remainder are left in the result registers.

name: multiply_low_32_bits
description: Multiplies two 32-bit values using 16-bit partial products and returns the low 32 bits of the product, while the returned low word holds the second input with its halves swapped.

name: invoke_global_function_pointer
description: Calls the function whose address is stored at a fixed offset in global data and then returns. The facts link it to the exec formatting call, but the code shows only the indirect call.

name: count_string_length_capped
description: Counts characters in a zero-terminated string by decrementing a 16-bit counter for each non-zero byte, stopping at the terminator or when the counter runs out, and returns the count.

name: find_character_in_string
description: Scans a zero-terminated string for the given byte and returns a pointer to its first occurrence, or a null pointer when the terminator comes first.

name: return_constant_zero
description: Returns zero with no other work.

name: copy_c_string
description: Copies bytes from a source pointer to a destination pointer, advancing both, and includes the zero terminator in the copy.

name: append_c_string
description: Moves to the terminator of the destination string, then copies the source bytes, including their terminator, onto the end of it.

name: compare_strings_up_to_count
description: Compares two byte strings for at most a given number of bytes, returning zero when they match up to that limit or the terminator and one when they differ.

name: return_constant_one
description: Returns one with no other work.

name: scan_string_with_limit
description: Walks a byte string for at most a given count of characters. When it reaches the terminator it calls a second routine before returning.

name: call_routine_and_return
description: Calls a second routine with no arguments and returns, doing no other work.

name: copy_string_with_zero_padding
description: Copies bytes from a source to a destination until a zero byte has been copied, then fills the rest of the given count with zero bytes.

name: initialize_list_header
description: Sets the first word of a block to point four bytes into itself, clears the second word, and stores the block's own address in the third word.

name: validate_and_process_entry
description: Returns success for an empty entry. Otherwise it checks the entry through a library routine and, if that passes, calls a second routine and processes a field of the entry through a third, returning the status of the last call.

name: walk_entry_list_checking_fields
description: Walks a linked list of entries, checking each one through a library routine and checking the buffer named in its second field, with a size taken from a byte in the entry. Returns one when the whole list passes and zero at the first failure.

name: return_constant_one
description: Returns one with no other work.

name: return_constant_zero
description: Returns zero with no other work.

name: allocate_linked_record
description: When its last argument is nonzero, allocates a 20-byte record and fills in its fields through several library calls, returning the record on success or minus one on failure. It returns zero when the last argument is zero.

name: return_constant_minus_one
description: Returns minus one with no other work.

name: build_linked_entry_chain
description: Walks a chain of entries, allocating a 16-byte record for each step and a buffer sized from a byte in the record, and linking each record to the next through library calls. Returns minus one if a call fails.

name: find_chain_tail_entry
description: Allocates and links entries in a chain through library calls, returning the entry whose link field is empty, or minus one when a call fails.

name: return_without_action
description: Returns immediately without any work, so calling it has no effect.

name: return_constant_minus_one
description: Returns minus one with no other work.

name: copy_block_and_invoke_callback
description: When the output pointer is non-null, copies sixteen 32-bit words from a fixed area of the program's data into it, then calls the function pointer held in a register. The routine belongs to the EndCLI program.

name: initialize_globals_and_start
description: Clears a large block of program globals to zero, saves the base pointers, optionally calls a library routine, and then calls one of two follow-up routines depending on the result of another library call.

name: setup_handles_and_resources
description: Opens two handles from global data, runs a sequence of setup calls using global configuration and fixed sizes, and then releases the handles through further calls. Its text references name the graphics and intuition libraries and the program's save and data files.

name: copy_file_in_blocks
description: Opens source and destination files from the path given, copies data in blocks of up to 32768 bytes until the source is exhausted, then closes both. Failures such as an unopened file or a full disk are reported through message routines.

name: write_data_in_blocks
description: Opens a destination file in the path given and writes a total number of bytes in blocks of up to 32768 bytes, checking each write and reporting a full disk or a file that cannot be created.

name: lock_program_directory_path
description: Locks the program directory path, falling back to a second lock when the first fails, then allocates a 512-byte block through a library call and stores it in global data.

name: transfer_block_with_delay
description: When a handle is open and the length argument is nonzero, issues a series of calls on the handle, pauses briefly through a delay call, and then runs its cleanup calls. Otherwise it only runs the cleanup calls.

name: configure_port_and_transfer
description: Opens a port from global data, issues a long run of configuration and transfer calls with fixed parameters on it, and reports progress text that includes the number of bytes transferred.

name: close_handle_if_open
description: When its stored handle is non-null, releases that handle through a library call and clears the stored value.

name: issue_fixed_handle_calls
description: Issues four parameterised calls on a stored handle using fixed codes and sizes, and passes a value from another routine into the last call along with its argument.

name: accumulate_and_report_offset
description: Adds its argument to a global running counter, then issues two calls on a stored handle, one of which uses the value returned by another routine.

name: forward_argument_to_routine
description: Passes its single argument on to another routine and returns, adding no further work.

name: initialize_disk_port
description: Stores its two arguments in global fields, clears a status field, and tries to create a message port. If creation fails it reports a fatal initialization error through a message routine.

name: store_two_values_and_clear
description: Stores its two arguments in fixed fields of the global block and clears a third field.

name: store_value_and_reset_count
description: Stores its argument in a fixed field of the global block and clears a second field.

name: write_blocks_in_chunks
description: Writes a requested number of bytes in 512-byte chunks: it first fills the current block, then writes whole blocks, and finally any partial remainder, updating the stored position after each write.

name: write_full_blocks_from_index
description: Works out a starting block index from stored position values, then writes successive 512-byte blocks from the source buffer, advancing the position each time while the remaining length is positive.

name: copy_pending_blocks
description: Loops over pending blocks in 512-byte steps, calling a routine for each and advancing a position counter, until the remaining length is no longer positive.

name: flush_or_close_pending_handle
description: If a pending handle is set it passes that handle to one routine. Otherwise, when a stored file handle exists, it performs two calls and then releases the handle through another routine.

name: seek_and_read_block
description: Updates a position field from stored offsets, then either transfers through a stored handle or, when the position has changed, seeks to the computed block.

name: queue_device_request
description: Fills a request structure with a command code, a 512-byte length, a buffer address and a computed offset, and then submits it through a routine.

name: queue_alternate_device_request
description: Fills a request structure for a 512-byte transfer the same way as its sibling routine, but with a different command code, then submits it through a routine.

name: wait_for_disk_insertion
description: Loops while a status byte reports a disk change, prompting for the data disk and waiting until a routine reports it present, and returns once the status byte is clear.

name: read_header_and_compare
description: Saves a block of state words, issues a read request for a 512-byte block, compares the result with a global string and restores the saved state, returning one on a match and zero otherwise.

name: queue_end_request
description: Sets the request command to a fourth variant and submits it through a routine.

name: queue_command_if_idle
description: When no pending handle is stored, sets the request command to code nine with zero length and submits it through a routine.

name: reset_and_return_field
description: Sets a global field to minus one and returns the value of a second field.

name: clear_and_write_header_bytes
description: Clears a 132-byte local buffer, copies a string into its tail, sets two header bytes, and writes its first 32 bytes through a routine.

name: fill_bytes_with_value
description: Stores a given byte into consecutive memory locations, counting down a 32-bit length that is split across two 16-bit halves.

name: return_without_action
description: Returns immediately without any work, so calling it has no effect.

name: allocate_port_request_block
description: Allocates a block sized from a global table entry, initializes its header fields, then links it to a stored value or passes it to a library routine. It returns early if the allocation fails.

name: tokenize_command_line
description: Splits a text line into tokens separated by spaces, tabs or line breaks, honoring double-quoted sections in which doubled quote characters stand for one quote. It terminates each token and builds an array of pointers to the tokens.

name: copy_limited_string_with_pad
description: Copies bytes from a source string into a destination for up to a given count, stopping early at a zero byte, then fills the rest of the count with zero bytes. It returns the destination pointer.

name: move_memory_block
description: Copies a block of bytes from one address to another in forward or backward order, so overlapping regions are preserved. It does nothing when the two addresses are equal.

name: append_limited_string
description: Moves to the end of the destination string and appends source bytes up to a fixed maximum length of 32766 bytes, adding a terminator when the source is cut short.

name: append_string_with_count
description: Finds the end of the destination string and appends source bytes after it up to a given count, adding a terminator when the source is cut short.

name: compare_byte_strings
description: Compares two zero-terminated byte strings character by character up to a fixed length limit, returning minus one when the first is smaller, one when it is larger and zero when they are equal.

name: copy_string_to_buffer
description: Copies bytes from a source string into a buffer until and including the zero terminator, and returns the buffer pointer.

name: open_icon_library_and_lookup
description: Opens the icon library by name, looks up an entry through library calls, and if that succeeds stores the resolved entry pointers in the caller's structure before closing the library.

name: format_into_global_buffer
description: Stores its first argument as the write position in global data, then runs the formatting routine on the caller's arguments and terminates the buffer with a zero byte.

name: format_into_global_buffer
description: Stores its first argument as the write position in global data, then runs the formatting routine on the caller's arguments and terminates the buffer with a zero byte.

name: append_byte_to_global_buffer
description: Writes one byte at the current global write position, advances that position, and returns the byte.

name: format_integer_as_string
description: Writes a number's digits into a buffer working backward from the end, using a table of digit characters, and adds a minus sign when the value is negative. It returns the position of the first character written.

name: format_printf_style_text
description: Walks a format string, sending literal characters through a callback and expanding each percent specifier for flags, width, precision and conversions such as character, string, decimal, octal, unsigned and hexadecimal values. It returns the number of characters produced, or minus one when the callback fails.

name: divide_with_sign_correction
description: Sets the sign of the result from the signs of its two inputs, calls a division routine, negates the quotient when the signs differ, and returns it with the second input.

name: negate_result_if_negative
description: Calls a routine and negates the value it leaves in its second register when the first input is negative, returning that value together with the second input.

name: call_and_return_pair
description: Calls another routine and returns its second output word paired with the original second input.

name: forward_call_and_return
description: Calls another routine with no arguments and returns, doing no other work. The decompiled output shows this call as a self-call, so the true target is unclear.

name: divide_32_bit_with_remainder
description: Divides a 32-bit unsigned value by a 32-bit divisor, using shift-and-subtract steps when the divisor exceeds 16 bits and two 16-bit divisions otherwise, returning quotient and remainder as a pair.

name: compute_string_length
description: Counts the bytes in a zero-terminated string, excluding the terminator, and returns that count. It does not modify memory.

name: invoke_callback_then_forward
description: Calls a stored callback function when one is set, then passes its argument on to a further routine.

name: release_program_resources
description: Releases in turn a table of allocated entries, a set of blocks and handles held in globals, and library or device resources, skipping any that are unset.

name: close_indexed_handle
description: Looks up a handle by index in a stored table, sets an error state when the index is out of range or the entry is empty, and otherwise releases the handle and clears its entry.

name: multiply_32_bit_values
description: Multiplies two 32-bit values from their 16-bit halves, producing the low 32 bits of the product, and returns it together with the second input.

name: close_handle_via_library
description: Jumps to the library's close function through a library base stored in global data.

name: open_via_library
description: Jumps to the library's open function through a library base stored in global data.

name: jump_to_library_function
description: Jumps to a library function through a library base held in global data, so the library routine receives the caller's arguments and returns directly to the caller.

name: allocate_message_block
description: Allocates a message block of a fixed size through a library call, fills in several of its fields from its arguments, and returns the block, or zero when allocation fails.

name: reset_message_block
description: Releases any message attached to the block, sets its status byte and a 32-bit field to all ones, then calls routines with a stored byte and a fixed code to finish.

name: jump_to_library_function
description: Jumps to a library function through a library base held in global data, so the library routine receives the caller's arguments and returns directly to the caller.

name: jump_to_library_function

name: jump_to_library_function
description: Jumps to a library function through a library base held in global data, so the library routine receives the caller's arguments and returns directly to the caller.

name: initialize_globals_and_start
description: Clears a large block of program globals to zero, saves the base pointers, optionally calls a library routine, and then calls one of two follow-up routines depending on the result of another library call.

name: initialize_memory_and_run_loop
description: Initializes a program counter and allocates a memory block sized from a query of available memory, checking it against a minimum amount. It sets up several buffers and then loops indefinitely, reporting 'Not enough memory' when the allocation fails.

name: handle_input_events_for_board
description: Reads input messages in a loop and dispatches each code: it stores pointer coordinates and selections in global data, sends board updates, and returns status codes such as 6 or 4099 to its caller. The routine references the text 'Boards are not synchronized'.

name: run_staged_progress_updates
description: Runs a set of progress steps chosen by a stage counter: each stage above a threshold triggers its own routine, two stored values are passed to one of them, and a final routine call ends the sequence.

name: run_staged_progress_updates
description: Runs a set of progress steps chosen by a stage counter: each stage above a threshold triggers its own routine, two stored values are passed to one of them, and a final routine call ends the sequence.

name: consume_pending_text_flag
description: If a pending flag is set, it calls a routine to handle it, clears the flag, calls another routine, and returns the address of a stored text buffer. Otherwise it returns zero.

name: return_constant_zero
description: Returns zero with no other work.

name: build_square_attribute_table
description: Walks the 64 board squares and, for each one, looks up its piece type and colour and packs a state code combining the piece code, colour and occupancy bits into a table entry. Empty squares are stored as zero.

name: fill_square_attribute_entries
description: Continues filling the 64-entry square attribute table from this entry point, packing each square's piece type, colour and occupancy bits and storing zero for empty squares. It returns once all 64 entries are stored.

name: fill_square_attribute_entries
description: Continues filling the 64-entry square attribute table from this entry point, packing each square's piece type, colour and occupancy bits and storing zero for empty squares. It returns once all 64 entries are stored.

name: fill_square_attribute_entries
description: Continues filling the 64-entry square attribute table from this entry point, packing each square's piece type, colour and occupancy bits and storing zero for empty squares. It returns once all 64 entries are stored.

description: Continues filling the 64-entry square attribute table from this entry point, packing each square's piece type, colour and occupancy bits and storing zero for empty squares. It returns once all 64 entries are stored.

description: Continues filling the 64-entry square attribute table from this entry point, packing each square's piece type, colour and occupancy bits and storing zero for empty squares. It returns once all 64 entries are stored.

name: fill_square_attribute_entries

name: fill_square_attribute_entries
description: Continues filling the 64-entry square attribute table from this entry point, packing each square's piece type, colour and occupancy bits and storing zero for empty squares. It returns once all 64 entries are stored.

name: build_row_bitmasks_for_colour
description: For each of eight rows, sets a bit for every square whose attribute matches the requested colour flag, and stores the eight row masks in a table.

name: clear_pending_selection_fields
description: Clears the first selection field when it is set, then clears the second selection field and calls routines to reset both.

name: initialize_board_session
description: Marks a state flag, saves and redirects a table pointer, and sets four buffer pointers 8000 bytes apart. It then calls routines for six entries, copies a 480-byte board image into place and loops over input events until a status code ends the loop.

name: run_board_input_loop
description: Copies a 480-byte board image into place and loops over input events, dispatching each code to branches that set or clear board state, copy the board image or call routines. It returns when the input routine reports its exit code.

name: process_pending_board_events
description: Loops over pending board-square entries, acting on each one that is marked as set by calling several routines and then clearing its flag, until the input routine reports that nothing further is pending.

name: reset_square_flags_and_wait
description: Sets a flag for each square in a loop, clears the associated entry and waits for input events from a routine, branching on the event code returned. It uses a stored value from global data as the piece value.

name: consume_pending_square_entry
description: If the currently selected square has a pending entry, it copies the entry's fields into the working state and clears the entry. It then loops waiting for input events and dispatches them.

name: clear_selection_and_refresh
description: If a selection is active, it passes the selection record to a routine and clears it. It then looks up a table entry from the current position and, when the position falls in a valid range, stores the matching table value as the new selection.

name: claim_free_selection_slot
description: Scans a fixed table of 32 records for an unused slot. When one is free it records the selection there and passes the matching record to a routine, and when none is free it reports an error code through a routine.

name: allocate_piece_slot_or_fail
description: Scans a table of 32 piece slots for a free entry. When none is free it reports the text 'Too many pieces.' through a routine, otherwise it records the slot and passes its record to a routine.

name: emit_selection_record
description: Stores its index as the current selection and passes the matching record to a routine, then loops waiting for input events and dispatching them as its sibling routines do.

name: clear_board_and_wait_input
description: Calls a routine, clears the 64 board entries and their companion flags, then loops waiting for input events and dispatching them.

name: restore_saved_board_snapshot
description: Copies 480 bytes from a saved board buffer into a working buffer, clears a state field, calls routines, and then loops over input events.

name: copy_board_bytes_then_wait
description: Copies bytes one at a time into a stored destination buffer and, once 480 bytes have been copied, runs routines and loops over input events.

name: dispatch_board_events_until_empty
description: Repeatedly fetches a value from an input routine and, while it is nonzero, processes it through the same event dispatch as its sibling routines.

name: start_board_session
description: Sets the state pointer to a stored block, clears two state fields and copies two arguments into global fields. It calls routines to set up the session and, when a field is nonzero, calls one more routine before clearing a flag.

name: run_board_event_loop
description: Runs an event loop that waits for input and dispatches each code. It returns once a specific termination code arrives and its follow-up call reports that no further data is available.

name: run_board_event_loop
description: Runs an event loop that waits for input and dispatches each code. It returns once a specific termination code arrives and its follow-up call reports that no further data is available.

name: forward_argument_to_routine
description: Passes its argument on to another routine and returns.

name: call_pointer_then_forward
description: Calls a function through a pointer stored in global data with its argument, then calls another routine and returns.

name: map_pointer_to_square
description: Converts a pointer position into a square index by searching two threshold tables for the column and row, then records the square as the current selection. When the position falls outside the board it clears the selection and reports through routines.

name: clear_selection_state
description: Passes two stored position fields to a routine, marks both as unset, optionally releases the active selection and copies several status bytes, then clears the remaining flags.

name: restore_selection_state
description: Copies several saved status bytes back into the working state fields and passes a fixed code to a routine.

name: read_line_into_buffer
description: Reads keyboard input into a buffer, echoing printable characters with an underscore cursor and handling backspace, until a carriage return. It stores at most the given maximum number of characters and returns the final length.

name: prompt_for_thinking_minutes
description: Prompts for the number of minutes to think, reads digit characters from input and converts them to an integer with a routine. It repeats until the value is between one and 10000, returning that value, or zero when the reply is negative.

name: read_minutes_number
description: Reads digit characters from a buffer, converting them to a number, and asks again until a value between one and 10000 is entered. It returns the accepted value.

name: read_minutes_number
description: Reads digit characters from a buffer, converting them to a number, and asks again until a value between one and 10000 is entered. It returns the accepted value.

name: return_without_action
description: Returns immediately without any work, so calling it has no effect.

name: show_message_until_click
description: Measures the text length, draws a message box sized to it, shows the text and waits for a specific input event before closing the box. The text passed in is what the player sees.

name: wait_for_pending_player_action
description: When either of two player slots is set to the value two, it sets a status field, runs a routine with a fixed code and loops while that state remains set, waiting for the action to clear it.

name: clear_wait_state
description: Clears a status word and a flag byte in global data.

name: read_and_send_command_line
description: Reads a line of up to 96 characters into a 40-byte stack buffer, terminates it with a carriage return and passes it to a routine. The same call is made whether or not the line is three plus signs.

name: send_ate_command_string
description: Places a four-byte string made of the letters A, T and E followed by a carriage return on the stack and passes it to a routine.

name: send_opponent_quit_message
description: Passes the global message string to a message routine. The string is associated with the text 'Your Opponent just quit'.

name: wait_for_selection_or_click
description: For a player slot set to the value two, it waits for an incoming byte. Otherwise it draws a selection area, waits for a click inside a range of screen positions and returns the byte associated with the clicked cell.

name: take_pending_byte
description: Returns a stored byte from global data and clears that stored value.

name: select_grid_cell_value
description: Draws a selection grid, waits for an input event at a position inside the grid bounds and returns the value stored in the table entry under that position.

name: select_grid_cell_value
description: Draws a selection grid, waits for an input event at a position inside the grid bounds and returns the value stored in the table entry under that position.

name: select_promotion_piece
description: Draws a grid of promotion choices, waits for a click inside the grid and returns the stored piece code under the click. The routine is associated with the text 'Promote pawn to?'.

name: wait_for_grid_click
description: Waits until the pointer position lies inside the grid bounds, marks the grid active and returns the table value for that position.

name: draw_nested_frames
description: Draws a sequence of nested rectangles by moving four edge coordinates inward on each step and drawing each frame, starting from the coordinates given in its arguments.

name: draw_square_with_cached_colour
description: When the requested colour index differs from the cached one, it stores the new index and calls a drawing routine with pen values taken from tables. An adjusted offset is used when the index is four.

name: initialize_graphics_buffers
description: Carves a block of memory into consecutive buffers using fixed and table-driven sizes, then calls routines to set up graphics resources and a list of 17 entries.

name: set_graphics_pointer_table
description: Stores six pointers into global fields, each at a fixed offset from a base block, so later routines can find the graphics and table areas.

name: initialize_board_tables
description: Clears six selection flags and eight marker bytes, then loads one of two sets of pointer tables depending on a state flag and calls routines to set up the display.

name: load_default_board_tables
description: Calls routines to draw the board, then stores a fixed set of five table pointers and makes one further call.

name: xor_scrambled_board_image
description: Calls a routine, then XORs 39960 bytes of data with the same data shifted forward by 40 bytes, one byte at a time.

name: save_board_pointer_state
description: Copies a set of global pointers and small state values into a saved-state block for later restoration.

name: restore_board_pointer_state
description: Copies the saved pointer and state values back into their global fields.

name: save_secondary_pointer_state
description: Copies a second set of global pointer and state values into a saved-state block at different offsets.

name: return_without_action
description: Returns immediately without any work, so calling it has no effect.

name: xor_piece_bitmap_rows
description: For each entry in a list of pieces, records pointers into a table, calls a routine with a size derived from width, height and five bitplanes, and XOR-combines source bitmap rows into the destination. It advances through the list until the terminator.

name: build_piece_sprite_table
description: Clears a 256-entry index table, computes per-piece sprite offsets from a list of pieces and their bitplane sizes, and reserves memory for each sprite while adjusting the running totals.

name: compact_sprite_entries
description: Removes a sprite entry from its list by copying the remaining entries down and adjusting the stored pointers and sizes of the entries that follow.

name: compact_sprite_list_tail
description: Adjusts the stored pointers and sizes of the list entries after a removed sprite, copies the remaining list down and updates the total in global data.

name: shift_sprite_entries
description: Moves the remaining sprite list entries down over a removed entry, adjusting their stored pointers, then updates the running total.

name: release_sprite_block
